abstract: the graviton self-energy $-i [\mbox{}^{μν} σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ is the 1pi 2-point function of quantum gravity. it can be used to quantum-correct the linearized einstein equation in order to infer quantum corrections to gravitational radiation and to the force of gravity. as long as the two points are non-coincident, the graviton self-energy does not need regularization at 1-loop order, however, solving the 1-loop effective field equations requires integrating $[\mbox{}^{μν} σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ over ${x'}^μ$, including ${x'}^μ = x^μ$. to facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and bphz renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de sitter background, in the simplest gauge. we then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the newtonian potential. although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.

title: a singularity theorem for quasi-topological gravities
abstract: quasi-topological theories of gravity have recently attracted substantial attention as several theories in this class have a non-singular black hole as a vacuum and spherically symmetric solution. this motivates the expectation that these theories can provide a resolution to the singularity problem and a description of black holes cores. the known solutions, however, possess a cauchy horizon which denotes the end of predictability of the theory, as the initial data do not determine a unique continuation past this type of horizon. in this paper, we show that penrose singularity theorem can be extended to all the known classes of quasi-topological theories that have non-singular black holes as solutions. we prove that spherical collapse satisfying the null energy condition necessarily leads to future null geodesic incompleteness once a trapped sphere forms. this implies that the lack of predictability of the theories is not an artefact of vacuum solutions and these theories are as problematic as general relativity for the dynamical studies of black hole interiors.

title: static vacuum geometry encodes gravitational collapse and cosmology
abstract: we show that, within covariant hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational hamiltonian. we further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. these conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.

title: gravitational-wave signal from a short grb relativistic mhd jet
abstract: we analyze the gravitational-wave (gw) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (mhd) simulation of a short grb jet with parameters corresponding to those of grb 170817a. the signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the grbs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized einstein equations of an mhd simulation. separating the gw signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. the waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the grb duration. a pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the gw signal can reveal processes deep in the grb engine that cannot be observed otherwise. the signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. the total radiated gw energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal e}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to gw170817 are marginally detectable by decigo from up to 10 mpc and by the einstein telescope from 1 mpc. the injected poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. an engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some grb models, would substantially increase the gw energy and detectability.

title: cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed einstein-yang-mills-higgs field theory: analytic treatment
abstract: non-abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the einstein-yang-mills-higgs field theory. the onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged reissner-nordström black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. in the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the einstein-yang-mills-higgs theory. in particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{μ_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $μ\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the yang-mills field due to the higgs effect). interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${μ_{k+1}/{μ_{k}}}=e^{-{{2π}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.

title: first law of thermodynamics for interacting charged black holes and applications
abstract: we derive a mass variation identity expressing the first law of black hole thermodynamics for asymptotically flat, stationary, axisymmetric einstein-maxwell solutions with multiple electrically charged horizons and finite conical axis singularities. under the stated asymptotic and parameter regularity hypotheses, the identity holds for independent variations of all parameters within families of fixed horizon types. on the all-degenerate family, a correction to the adm mass defines a scalar function whose derivatives with respect to angular momenta are the horizon angular velocities. at the majumdar-papapetrou family, its angular momentum hessian is positive definite. combining the first variation identity with a separate theorem on the sign of the conical parameters shows that this hessian is nondecreasing in the positive-semidefinite order along admissible paths of increasing weyl gaps at fixed positive charges.

title: hidden by exponential screening: the invisibility of the dymnikova black hole de sitter core to accretion observables
abstract: the dymnikova spacetime replaces the schwarzschild singularity with a de sitter core, and its lapse deviates from schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2m)}$. whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. we address it with grhd simulations of bhl accretion onto dymnikova bh for six values of the critical length, $0.1m\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1m$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. all runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. the dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7m$. because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. the time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3m)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0m$ and $31.6\pm0.4m)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. accretion onto a dymnikova bh is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. more broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

title: charge-activated birefringence and shadow mimicry around reissner-nordström black holes
abstract: we discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the einstein tensor around a reissner-nordström black hole. changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. the coupling makes the two parity looks differently. it separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. however changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. they require both nonzero charge and coupling. at weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. negative coupling reverses these trends. the backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. it is entirely helicity reversed. for the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. we can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. a comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

title: spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: stabilizing the unstable
abstract: the spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. we study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on reissner--nordström and reissner--nordström--de sitter backgrounds. a localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. in the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. by searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. the real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. in de sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. after stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. a prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

title: integrable mass of kerr-newman-bertotti-robinson black hole
abstract: the nontrivial asymptotic structure of rotating black holes in the bertotti-robinson universe complicates a direct determination of their conserved mass, leading previous studies to rely on a priori thermodynamic input. we address this long-standing problem using integrability methods, establish local analytic existence and uniqueness via the cauchy-kovalevskaja theorem, and obtain a closed expression via a rescaled recurrence whose termination is proved at all orders. the resulting kerr-newman-bertotti-robinson mass coincides with the expression previously derived using the canonical first law identity and reproduces the masses of both kerr-bertotti-robinson subcases. with the mass thus fixed without invoking thermodynamic relations for the first time, we rigorously establish the first law of black-hole thermodynamics and the smarr formula for a whole family of kerr-bertotti-robinson black holes suitable for future applications.

title: exact regular planar black holes solutions in bumblebee gravity
abstract: we discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. we consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. the field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. analytical expressions for this functions has been found. this solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.

title: exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
abstract: the static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the schwarzschild geometry. we derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the schwarzschild background. we fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. the result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.

title: surrogate model of gravitational waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries based on the hybridization of wasabi-c inspirals with numerical relativity waveforms
abstract: with the incorporation of aligned-spin dynamics into self-force waveform models, such as the wasabi-c inspiral model, and with the release of the sxs collaboration's third public catalog of nr simulations, the gravitational waveform modeling community has made significant advances in the modeling of spinning, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries. in light of these developments, we present wasabinrhybsur2dq15, the first surrogate model to incorporate information from self-force theory, post-newtonian theory, and numerical relativity. the model is trained on 65 hybrid waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries with mass ratios spanning 1:1.25 to 1:20 and aligned-spins for the primary black hole ranging -0.5 to 0.5. the hybrid waveforms are generated from a set of wasabi-c inspirals and nr waveforms from the third sxs public catalog. the model covers the parameter domain $1.25 \leq q \leq 15$ and $|χ_{1z}| \leq 0.5$, and includes the $(2,2),\, (2,1),\, (3,3),\, (4,4),$ and $(5,5)$ spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes. the model also spans the entire ligo-virgo-kagra (lvk) frequency band (with $f_{\text{low}}=20$ hz) for total masses $m \gtrsim 111.5\,m_{\odot}$. we find that the wasabinrhybsur2dq15 model faithfully reproduces the hybrid waveforms with mismatches less than $10^{-3}$ for total masses in the range $80\,m_{\odot} \leq m \leq 300\,m_{\odot}$.

title: tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
abstract: the direct wave component of black hole (bh) ringdown, revealed through quasinormal-mode filters, carries a non-quasinormal-mode imprint of the plunging perturber's dynamics. however, the connection between the source trajectory and the observed direct wave remains incompletely understood. we first show that the full waveform filtered by the frequency-dependent black hole response gives a substantially more localized kernel than the standard rational filter approach. we then show that analytically continuing the teukolsky source variables to complex coordinates allows for a semianalytic direct wave which closely reproduces numerical integration throughout the entire plunge. our generalized steepest-descent method clarifies how coherent emission shapes the imprint of source dynamics on the observed direct wave beyond the light-cone picture.

title: mercury (hg): a relativistic $n$-body simulation for horndeski gravity
abstract: we present mercury, a relativistic $n$-body code for cosmological simulations in the $α$-basis formulation of horndeski gravity. mercury extends a particle-mesh scheme by incorporating the dynamics of the additional scalar degree of freedom and the corresponding modified einstein equations, expressed in terms of the time-dependent functions $α_{\rm k}, α_{\rm b}, α_{\rm m}, α_{\rm t}$ and the effective planck mass $m_*^2$. this generalises our previous implementation of horndeski subclass models, namely $k$-essence and kinetic gravity braiding (kgb), to the general linear horndeski $α$-basis. the code evolves the additional scalar degree of freedom and its effective stress--energy tensor alongside the nonlinear matter and metric fields, so that nonlinear structure formation sources the scalar-field evolution and feeds back on the gravitational potentials. through its interface with hi_class, mercury supports both phenomenological $α$-function parametrisations and covariant horndeski theories; we demonstrate the latter using nkgb, the cubic galileon, and brans--dicke models. we validate the implementation against hi_class in the linear regime and recover the expected nonlinear $k$-essence and kgb limits. for the luminal horndeski models considered here, we show how a running effective planck mass generates gravitational slip through the scalar anisotropic stress and modifies the friction terms governing the vector and tensor metric perturbations. the evolution of $m_*^2$ also modifies the normalisation and scale dependence of the effective dark-energy density contrast, leaving a corresponding imprint on its power spectrum. the present framework provides an intermediate step towards nonlinear horndeski simulations, in which nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening effects can be incorporated consistently within the same relativistic framework.
